4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Ciara Walda, the Minister of Education, joined us on the balcony, dressed in a sky-blue pantsuit. Her preference for trousers over dresses had made her the subject of much Palace gossip, but it didn't seem to bother her in the slightest.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: While I was mesmerized by the scenery, Paskal Beniwoll walked up to me.

6.speaker: Ciara Walda
6.text: “Hopelessness and a lack of opportunities can drive people to extreme solutions. We're seeing increased crime, domestic violence, and yes, rising inequality between men and women..."

7.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
7.text: “There is another subject I want to mention. I have been working on improving the rights of workers in our country and have proposed a draft bill that is currently being reviewed by our party.”

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: The meeting room was already prepared for state business. Small gifts for each of us had been placed on the table by the municipality. We took our seats.

10.speaker: Player
10.text: “Let's start with your health overview, Paskal.”

11.speaker: Player
11.text: “Tell me more about your plans, Ciara.”

16.speaker: Player
16.text: “How many doctors and nurses are employed?”

17.speaker: Player
17.text: “How many hospital beds are there per ten thousand citizens?”

18.speaker: Player
18.text: “What's the life expectancy and mortality rates?”

28.speaker: Player
28.text: “Tell me about the difference between urban and rural education.”

29.speaker: Player
29.text: “What is the literacy rate of Sordland?”

33.speaker: Player
33.text: “How many students and teachers do we have?”

40.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
40.text: “We have 31,594 doctors and 73,680 nurses working for the Ministry of Health. This is a high number. What I think is--”

41.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
41.text: “There are ten beds per ten thousand citizens. Compared to most of our neighbors, this is a very good number."

42.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
42.text: “Our life expectancy is 65 years. The infant mortality rate is a worrying 121 per one thousand births, while our maternal mortality is at 5 per thousand.”

43.speaker: Ciara Walda
43.text: “Currently there are about five million students. Three million in primary education, one million in secondary and one million in tertiary. There are 155,316 teachers.”

44.speaker: Ciara Walda
44.text: “The literacy rate of Sordland is at eighty percent. This is a very good indicator for future growth, but it needs to increase. It's also far lower among girls than boys.”

45.speaker: Ciara Walda
45.text: “Urban areas have three times the number of schools per ten thousand people compared to rural areas. Rural areas also suffer from a lack of teachers.”

46.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
46.text: “I am doing my best to ensure that citizens of all ages receive the best healthcare they can. I also personally want to solve our high infant and maternal mortality problem.”

47.speaker: Ciara Walda
47.text: “I don't want to be rude, but out of those numbers. how many are in urban and in rural areas?”

50.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
50.text: “That's not a problem. The number of doctors per ten thousand citizens is far lower in rural areas compared to urban areas.”

51.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
51.text: “The data shows that per ten thousand people in urban areas there are about eleven doctors, while in rural areas there are only three.”

54.speaker: Player
54.text: “I want to hear about the healthcare system.”

57.speaker: Ciara Walda
57.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_PSnW_Listened_Education_Students"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_PSnW_Listened_Education_Literacy"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_PSnW_Listened_Education_UrbanRural"] == true) == false

60.speaker: Ciara Walda
60.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_PSnW_Listened_Health_DoctorsNurses"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_PSnW_Listened_Health_Beds"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_PSnW_Listened_Health_LifeMortality"] == true) == false

61.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
61.text: “Our amount of beds is higher than the countries of Agnolia and Wehlen, but we obviously can't match Lespia or Valgsland.”

63.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
63.text: “I assure you that we are doing everything we can to save mothers and their newborns.”

64.speaker: Player
64.text: “I expect nothing but your best efforts to improve the situation.”

66.speaker: Player
66.text: “I agree. We must do everything we can.”

67.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
67.text: “We are working very hard on improving the quality of the services.”

69.speaker: Narrator
69.text: Ciara stood up and moved towards the window. She took a deep breath.

70.speaker: Ciara Walda
70.text: “My highest priority is to get enough funding to be able to build schools in rural areas while I cleanse our educational system of its nationalistic indoctrination and sexist teachings."

73.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
73.text: “Sordland is full of young and bright minds.”

74.speaker: Player
74.text: “We should keep striving to make education available for all.”

75.speaker: Player
75.text: “Our country is indeed full of potential.”

76.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
76.text: “If I remember correctly, the most illiterate areas are Bergia and Agnland.”

77.speaker: Ciara Walda
77.text: “That is correct. Although Lachaven skews the statistics for the Nargis region, which also has a vast number of illiterate citizens. This underlines my point about the lack of access to education."

79.speaker: Player
79.text: “I can imagine teachers not preferring desolate areas.”

81.speaker: Ciara Walda
81.text: “This is one of the most important problems we face, if not the most important. A huge part of the population is forgotten in terms of welfare.”

84.speaker: Player
84.text: “I want to hear about the education system.”

87.speaker: Player
87.text: “I hope both of you are preparing your reform plans for improvement.”

88.speaker: Ciara Walda
88.text: “Look at this impoverished city. The streets full of potholes, the hospital barely functioning, the school half open.”

90.speaker: Ciara Walda
90.text: “This is not just about Soll or even Alphonso failing. This decay in Sordland's forgotten regions has been going on for many decades due to structural corruption, which is fueled by capitalism.”

92.speaker: Player
92.text: “We are here to change that trend and to provide for the people.”

93.speaker: Player
93.text: “Tarquin Soll did more for the country than any of us.”

94.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
94.text: “There is not much to be said, sir. I agree with Ciara, but it is also Gus Manger's job to improve these areas.”

95.speaker: Ciara Walda
95.text: “It's the responsibility of each and every one of us.”

96.speaker: Ciara Walda
96.text: “That remains to be seen. I'm working on the new education system, and your support would be welcome.”

97.speaker: Ciara Walda
97.text: “Really? I must agree to disagree then.”

98.speaker: Ciara Walda
98.text: “Did we cover all the necessary subjects?”

99.speaker: Ciara Walda
99.text: “I do hope we won't repeat the same mistakes again and again. Have a good day, Mr. President.”

100.speaker: Narrator
100.text: The ministers left, and I prepared to leave for other official business in the city. The Gasom meeting was just one of the many events I was scheduled to attend over the next few days.

101.speaker: Narrator
101.text: By looking at the citizens’ attire, it was easy to understand the current state of Narbel. Some people were wearing clothes a few sizes too large. Some kids did not even have shoes. Yet there was hope in their eyes.

103.speaker: Ciara Walda
103.text: “My plans require an increase in the government budget. I aim to solve the problems we highlighted with the allocated money.”

104.speaker: Ciara Walda
104.text: “By building schools in these less fortunate rural areas and through fundamental changes to the education system, I will unlock the potential of all our children. Boys and girls alike."

105.speaker: Player
105.text: "Interesting. I thought our problem was with the quality of education in Sordland as a whole.”

106.speaker: Player
106.text: “Improving the situation in rural areas is indeed a good idea.”

107.speaker: Ciara Walda
107.text: “It's an investment in the future of Sordland. Imagine unlocking the full, untapped potential of our youth. The knowledge and wealth they will generate.”

108.speaker: Ciara Walda
108.text: “Our statistics show the disparity between urban and rural education. We can either do something about it, or wait until things get worse.”

109.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
109.text: “Wouldn't a promotion of private education help create additional funds?”

110.speaker: Ciara Walda
110.text: “Yes, but at what cost? I'm not a supporter of the private sector in education. At the end of the day, they are focused on profit first.”

112.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
112.text: “I personally want to improve the low quality of healthcare in the rural areas.”

113.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
113.text: “I can do more with an increased budget. Additionally, a privatization plan to promote private investments in the healthcare system could allocate extra funds.”

114.speaker: Player
114.text: “Isn't access to healthcare in rural areas an issue?”

115.speaker: Player
115.text: “Improving the quality of healthcare in less fortunate areas should be our highest priority.”

116.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
116.text: “Access is an issue, but not as critical as improving the quality in these areas. The lack of experienced personnel and equipment causes poor treatment, resulting in many deaths.”

117.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
117.text: “Exactly. It would directly diminish our depressingly high infant and maternal mortality situation. Besides, such a push would also have economic benefits.”

118.speaker: Player
118.text: “Lileas Graf will take care of crime. She's an expert on the subject."

119.speaker: Player
119.text: “Those issues must be tackled from different directions. We need to engage it holistically.”

120.speaker: Player
120.text: “If only we could stop the recession, create jobs and growth...”

121.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
121.text: “I'm planning to help by using an increased budget to improve the quality of healthcare.”

122.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
122.text: “She is certainly a proven administrator. From what I heard she reduced crime in Arvory by 40% during her mayoral term.”

123.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
123.text: “The economic situation does play a huge role in living standards. Our urban and rural disparities are stark, and the recession hit the weakest harder.”

124.speaker: Ciara Walda
124.text: “I don't think brute force will get us anywhere. Look at where the tight grip of Tarquin Soll got us.”

125.speaker: Ciara Walda
125.text: "That could prove useful, but we need to be doing a lot more. Education has similar issues.”

126.speaker: Ciara Walda
126.text: “We can't fix the economy by ourselves. We have to educate the people and let them create new opportunities too.”

127.speaker: Ciara Walda
127.text: “Agnolia and Wehlen should hardly be used as a standard, but it is good to know we aren't in a massive health crisis. Yet.”

128.speaker: Ciara Walda
128.text: “I think there needs to be a change in what is being taught. We should help children to ask questions and educate themselves.”

129.speaker: Narrator
129.text: Ciara sat back down and sighed.

130.speaker: Ciara Walda
130.text: “One way or another, we need change in Sordland. Greed and unchecked capitalism will not magically provide for the people.”

131.speaker: Player
131.text: “Tell me more about your plans, Ciara.”

132.speaker: Ciara Walda
132.text: “My expectation from our government is that we understand and focus on the needs of the people.”

147.speaker: Ciara Walda
147.text: “Sordish education is free, but we have a very outdated system that I want to reform. The other important issue is the lack of access to education in rural areas, especially for young girls. Your administration has the power to solve both problems."

148.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
148.text: “Sordland has a free healthcare system, except for a few private hospitals operating under it. Most of the populace receives adequate treatment. Health issues primarily appear in rural areas due to a lack of quality services.”

150.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
150.text: “I do hope to create competition and increase the quality of healthcare with the privatization effort.”

151.speaker: Ciara Walda
151.text: “But you must realize that privatizing our health care system would increase the price of treatment and make access worse for the average citizen.”

152.speaker: Ciara Walda
152.text: “Salaries for teachers are very low here. We need to increase their pay to give them more incentive."

153.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
153.text: “So, I created draft plans to increase the salary of doctors and to upgrade the equipment of the hospitals.”

154.speaker: Ciara Walda
154.text: “I am glad we see eye to eye on the issue.”

155.speaker: Player
155.text: “My intention is to help the working class.”

159.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
159.text: “Well put, Ms. Walda. I don't need to tell you about my own experiences with poverty. And you've been through similar hardships yourself, Mr. President.”

160.speaker: Ciara Walda
160.text: “If you look past the view, you can see the real problems.”

161.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
161.text: “Well put, Ms. Walda. I don't need to tell you about my own experiences with poverty. I'm sure you have similar stories, am I right, Mr. President?”

168.speaker: Player
168.text: “We knew less fortunate families, even though we belonged to the middle class ourselves.”

169.speaker: Player
169.text: "Thankfully, we never had any problems with money.”

170.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
170.text: “So, you could at least sympathize with the plight of these people.”

171.speaker: Ciara Walda
171.text: “You don't have to have been born poor to sympathize with the plight of the impoverished. Much as you don't have to have been born a woman to recognize Sordland's need for parity among the sexes.”

172.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
172.text: “You know the saying; you don't know what you have until it is taken from you.”

173.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
173.text: “Exactly. It feels as if there is no way out.”

174.speaker: Player
174.text: “It feels like the cards are stacked against you.”

175.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
175.text: “True but some lives are more difficult than others. Like ours was, and still is for hundreds of thousands in Sordland.”

176.speaker: Player
176.text: “We have all gone through difficult times.”

177.speaker: Ciara Walda
177.text: “As I was saying -- isn't it about time Holsord addressed this country's real issues? Rather than bowing to the wishes of the hawks and fearmongerers in the establishment, and diverting yet more resources to the military and law enforcement?”

178.speaker: Ciara Walda
178.text: “Our welfare, healthcare and education systems have been decaying since the recession. Sordland's poorer communities are losing hope."

179.speaker: Ciara Walda
179.text: “Sordland needs more schools full of children instead of barracks full of soldiers, more hospitals instead of police stations.”

180.speaker: Player
180.text: “The capital must be prioritised towards the resources that matter the most.”

181.speaker: Ciara Walda
181.text: “In other words, rural citizens with medical emergencies have to wait an embarassingly long time before they are treated.”

182.speaker: Ciara Walda
182.text: “One cannot be separated from the other, Mr. Rayne. The issues stem from the ideology."

183.speaker: Player
183.text: “Let's not get into an ideological debate. We need to focus on the issues.”

187.speaker: Ciara Walda
187.text: “Besides, it wouldn't fit into the planned economy President Rayne has decided to promote.”

188.speaker: Ciara Walda
188.text: “The decision not to promote more state control would cost the Sordish people dearly.”

189.speaker: Ciara Walda
189.text: “I don't want to sound cynical, but almost all governments keep making the same promises. We must show we are different through our actions.”

190.speaker: Ciara Walda
190.text: “It is the same play and the same book. The security complex in the country keeps driving the agenda as usual.”

191.speaker: Player
191.text: “We are elected representatives of our people and we will prioritize their needs.”

192.speaker: Player
192.text: “There are other significant issues that we need to focus on, like security.”

193.speaker: Player
193.text: “I appreciate your briefings and plans. We will re-convene at the budget meeting.”

195.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
195.text: “There have been a lot of negative developments lately.”

197.speaker: Ciara Walda
197.text: “See you at the meeting. I hope to see a change in direction.”

198.speaker: Ciara Walda
198.text: “Spectacular indeed. But if you look in the opposite direction, you will see what Soll's decades of neglect did to the city.”

199.speaker: Narrator
199.text: I arrived at the meeting room for my talk with Ciara and Paskal. Before beginning, I took a moment to appreciate the view from the balcony. The mountains of Narbel were completely covered with snow.

200.speaker: Player
200.text: “Whatever. I'd much rather be in Holsord right now.”

201.speaker: Ciara Walda
201.text: “Our presence here will show that we still remember Narbel and other forgotten areas of our country.”

202.speaker: Ciara Walda
202.text: “Most of the people living in Narbel are workers, farmers and their wives and children. They're breaking their backs for close to no pay, all thanks to greedy corporations.”

205.speaker: Player
205.text: “We can't really blame the companies. That's just how they work.”

206.speaker: Ciara Walda
206.text: “Yes we can. Similar companies are doing much better for their workers in United Contana and Arcasia.”

207.speaker: Narrator
207.text: As I made my way out, the weather was noticeably cold, but it didn’t keep a group of USP supporters from coming out to cheer us on the streets.

208.speaker: Narrator
208.text: They were excited to see their president in their city.

209.speaker: Player
209.text: “I personally promised that our health systems were to be improved in our term. I fully support you Paskal.”

213.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
213.text: “This is one of the reasons I'm optimistic about the upcoming budget debates. With enough funds, we can build new hospitals and expand the quality of our services.”

217.speaker: Player
217.text: “Our election mandate was to improve education. We will deliver on this.”

218.speaker: Ciara Walda
218.text: “This brings hope to the table, which needs to be followed by action. There is much to be done, but if we're given the budget, we can implement policies that push education to the next level.”

222.speaker: Player
222.text: “Welfare is my top priority. Both education and health will be improved significantly under this administration.”

223.speaker: Ciara Walda
223.text: “Exactly. Increasing law enforcement isn't something that reflects nicely on society, in comparison to services that people use every day."

224.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
224.text: “The people will rejoice if they see grand improvements in welfare. Our public opinion ratings will increase drastically.”

225.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
225.text: “It's getting a little cold out here. Shall we continue our discussion indoors?"

226.speaker: Player
226.text: “I agree. We need to improve the standards for our workers.”

227.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
227.text: “Mr. Clavin has already backed me and given his support. Sordland has fallen behind most countries on this subject and it is my responsibility to ensure this is not the case.”

228.speaker: Player
228.text: “There is always room for improvement and it is good to hear that you are pushing for it.”

229.speaker: Player
229.text: “We shouldn't upset the businesses who are already struggling to stay afloat in the crisis.”

230.speaker: Ciara Walda
230.text: “It also is a matter of life and death. Every decade we hear of some horrific accident due to employers' disregard for their workers' safety."

231.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
231.text: “Exactly. Sordland must provide for its own people to move forward.”

232.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
232.text: “Appreciate the kind words, Mr. President. I will not let you down.”

233.speaker: Ciara Walda
233.text: “Why would you turn away from the pro-labor cause when you yourself supported the Red Youth during your university years?”

234.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
234.text: “This wouldn't alter the balance of operational companies drastically. It would just punish them if they are treating their workers unfairly.”

241.speaker: Ciara Walda
241.text: “It has shown your dedication, but there are many years ahead of us. This is just the beginning of the journey.”

242.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
242.text: “No matter how small a step, it still is progress.”

243.speaker: Player
243.text: “Minister Walda, I have bailed out people in need instead of businesses. Trust me, my priorities are correct.”

244.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
244.text: “So, will you back the bill when it arrives on your desk, Mr. President?”

245.speaker: Player
245.text: “I would be very interested in supporting it once it is finished.”

247.speaker: Player
247.text: “To make a decision, I would need to evaluate the contents in detail.”

248.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
248.text: “Understandable. You will receive all the sections in an outline.”

249.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
249.text: “It is obvious that the military has been overfunded for a long time. Perhaps it is time to change this trend.”

250.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
250.text: “It is obvious that the military has been overfunded for a long time and you have promised to change this trend.”

254.speaker: Player
254.text: “Sounds like a costly bill for such a low-priority issue."

255.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
255.text: “If the very lives of our workers aren't a priority, than what is? Our administration should be able to set a budget aside for these types of improvements.”

256.speaker: Player
256.text: “I am not necessarily opposed to it. I'm sceptical.”

259.speaker: Ciara Walda
259.text: “One would hope ideals haven't changed as drastically.”

261.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
261.text: “Maybe by the time the bill is done, you will have changed your mind.”

262.speaker: Player
262.text: “I don't think this is the time for such a change. We have bigger issues to fix.”

282.speaker: Narrator
282.text: Paskal nodded gravely. This was a subject he knew quite a bit about himself. His best-known books were about the plight of Sordland's less fortunate, drawing from his own past growing up in squalor.

283.speaker: Narrator
283.text: My Minister of Health was, ironically, somewhat portly, having gained a few pounds since his breakthrough as a best-selling writer. But his authority on social affairs could not be questioned.

295.speaker: Player
295.text: “Thank you, Paskal. Your in-depth briefing is much appreciated.”

296.speaker: Player
296.text: “Thank you, Ciara. I can fill in the blanks from here.”

297.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
297.text: “Parity among the sexes shouldn't be our first priority. Look at how many high-ranking female politicians our country has."

300.speaker: Ciara Walda
300.text: "Think about how Lileas Graf got to her current position. I don't necessarily believe the rumors about her and Soll, but she never could have risen so high if she didn't parrot his cause."

301.speaker: Ciara Walda
301.text: "Gloria Tory -- is it an accident that the first female Assembly speaker is such a staunch conservative?"

302.speaker: Ciara Walda
302.text: "And then there was Alphonso's habit of promoting women to prominent positions to give Sordland a progressive sheen while accomplishing nothing in reality..."

303.speaker: Ciara Walda
303.text: "While women in places like Narbel are denied any opportunity to advance, the government can use a handful of female politicians from wealthy families -- myself included -- to pretend their only obstacle to success is their own lack of initiative."

304.speaker: Ciara Walda
304.text: "Meanwhile, those of us who don't use our clout to help powerful men stay in power are denigrated as angry spinsters... I ask you, Mr. President, does anyone care that your strategist Mr. Galade doesn't have a wife?"

308.speaker: Player
308.text: "I agree with you completely. Sordland's women deserve better."

310.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
310.text: "All right, Ciara. You've made your point."

314.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
314.text: "Nevertheless, it's worth acknowledging the corporation's significant contribution to job creation in Narbel and other poverty-stricken regions. Persuading the chairman to make concessions might prove to be a formidable task."

315.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
315.text: "One more thing. I wish to raise my concerns about your scheduled meeting with the Gasom chairman and former President, Mr. Alphonso."

316.speaker: Ciara Walda
316.text: "What is there to negotiate, Paskal? The standards for Gasom workers are already at rock bottom. President Rayne can and must demand better."

317.speaker: Player
317.text: "What good is job creation if the workers are treated poorly? Of course I'll demand better from Alphonso."

318.speaker: Player
318.text: "I know how slippery Alphonso can be. Bringing this up with him will indeed be a challenge."

319.speaker: Player
319.text: "If we do this right, we can find a solution that advances both the economy and the interests of laborers."

320.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
320.text: "I covered this topic extensively in one of my books. Confrontation, if not handled prudently, could exacerbate the challenges these workers face."

321.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
321.text: "Try a diplomatic approach. Deep down, I believe he wants what is best for the workers as well."

322.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
322.text: "That would be quite the impressive feat. You'd make headlines for it."

323.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
323.text: “This matter is close to my heart. I would personally be grateful if you are able to resolve the concerns raised by Katarina Horten and her fellow labor representatives.”

324.speaker: Ciara Walda
324.text: “It would be difficult to imagine a CEO like Alphonso giving benefits to workers without him personally gaining from it.”

325.speaker: Player
325.text: "In this world, nothing is truly free. I wouldn't anticipate anything less."

326.speaker: Player
326.text: "Gasom relies on us just as we rely on them. We can find a path to compromise."

327.speaker: Player
327.text: "Gasom has profited from the labor of workers for far too long. It's time for them to give back."

328.speaker: Ciara Walda
328.text: “We must be cautious about these seemingly generous offers. They usually come with hidden costs that further tip the scales in favor of the privileged few.”

329.speaker: Ciara Walda
329.text: “The middle way often sways perilously close to the status quo. We must ensure that any negotiations genuinely benefit the people and not just uphold the interests of corporate giants.”

330.speaker: Ciara Walda
330.text: “We shouldn't settle for anything less than a complete overhaul of the exploitative structures Gasom and its fellow corporations have built.”

331.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
331.text: "Thank you for your input, Ciara. But I will stress to President Rayne how important it is that the door to dialogue remain open."

332.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
332.text: "Ideology should never get in the way of bringing about tangible, lasting change."

333.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
333.text: "By negotiating with Alphonso and his company, you have an opportunity to secure better labor conditions for blue-collar Gasom employees. This could be a triumph for all of Narbel."

334.speaker: Player
334.text: "My foremost priorities lie in improving the economy. Once that is achieved, upward mobility will naturally follow suit."

335.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
335.text: "Economic improvements don't always automatically translate into greater happiness and well-being, Mr. President."

336.speaker: Player
336.text: "Considering our need for greater energy security, we might find ourselves forced to collaborate with him."

337.speaker: Ciara Walda
337.text: "Remember, these 'collaborations' usually come with strings attached. Often, they disproportionately favor corporations while placing the burden on the common people."

338.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
338.text: “We shall keep you no longer. Thank you both for the discussions."

339.speaker: Player
339.text: "I'm encouraged by the willingness of Mr. Manger and Mr. Alphonso to meet with me. It's a step forward."

340.speaker: Player
340.text: "I disagree. Only by holding firm to my convictions can I bring about the change Sordland needs."

341.speaker: Player
341.text: "I'm skeptical that these discussions with Gasom will lead to any meaningful change. We've seen empty promises before."

342.speaker: Player
